title: Structural, Optical, and Electrical Properties of ZnS Thin Films: Role of Cobalt Doping
content:
Spray-pyrolyzed Co-doped ZnS thin films exhibited tunable structural, optical, and electrical properties. Cobalt doping reduced the bandgap and resistivity while enhancing carrier concentration, highlighting the potential of these films for optoelectronic applications.


ABSTRACT

The undoped and cobalt (Co) doped ZnS films were prepared by the spray pyrolysis technique. The doping concentration of the films was altered at 1 at%, 2 at%, 3 at%, and 5 at%, respectively. The prepared films exhibited a cubic phase with a prominent peak corresponding to the (111) plane. The crystallite size of the films varied from 5.2 to 8.7 nm with the addition of cobalt. The lattice constant of the films was slightly deviated from that of the undoped film. The bandgap of the films was reduced from 3.9 to 3.7 eV with the incorporation of the cobalt. The Urbach energy of the ZnS films was deviated from 0.44 to 1.11 eV with cobalt doping. The resistivity and carrier concentration of the films varied from 3.1 × 103 to 0.16 × 103 ohm cm and 0.22 × 1015 to 2.27 × 1015 cm−3, respectively.
